title: Afternoon micro-playbook: docs fixes & sample app triage
body:
Context:
- Quick personal playbook for the afternoon: focus on a few high-leverage doc fixes and unblock the sample app that blocked the new tutorial release. Keep this small and actionable.

Top-level goal:
- Get tutorial v0.3 deployable: fix sample app startup, update docs for environment variables, and add one small example for batched inference.

Priority checklist (30 / 90 / 120 min buckets):
- 30m: reproduce locally, capture failure logs, and file clear minimal reproduction steps.
- 90m: patch sample app (hotfix), update quickstart snippet, add a tiny test.
- 120m: push PR, add note to tutorial page and call out in release notes.

Immediate repro steps I used:
1) git checkout feature/tutorial-quickstart
2) ./scripts/setup-local.sh --env=dev (this sets REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION)
3) cd examples/simple-chat && docker-compose up --build
4) error seen in logs: "ModelLoadError: incompatible quantization schema" on container model-server

Observations / hypotheses:
- The docker image used by examples/simple-chat is still pulling a GPU-optimized runtime tag (gpu-v2) that doesn't support the local CPU-only quantized model. Should default to cpu-compat tag.
- env var sample in README uses REDWOOD_REGION=eu-west-1 but the test harness expects us-east-1 (hardcoded in test_config). That caused intermittent failures for new devs.

Small fix plan (concrete):
- Change docker-compose image tag in examples/simple-chat from redwood/runtime:gpu-v2 to redwood/runtime:cpu-compat-2026-02-01. (1 file change)
- Update README env example: show both REDWOOD_REGION and REDWOOD_API_HOST with fallback comment.
- Add a smoke-check script examples/simple-chat/check-smoke.sh which waits for /health and asserts model-ready. Add to CI as flaky-gate.

Suggested docs wording (short snippet to paste):
- "If you're running locally without GPUs, use the cpu-compat runtime tag (redwood/runtime:cpu-compat-2026-02-01). This image is configured to run quantized CPU models and will avoid ModelLoadError seen with GPU-only images."

Risk notes / open questions:
- Does changing runtime tag affect Dedicated customers who rebase examples? Add a short note in examples/README: "Examples are intended for local dev and may not match Dedicated production images."
- Do we need to add a small CI job that runs examples in CPU mode on PRs? (Follow-up: ask SRE about CI budget)

PR checklist for the patch (pre-push):
- [ ] update docker-compose in examples/simple-chat
- [ ] update README env var section + short rationale line
- [ ] add check-smoke.sh + small test that exits non-zero if model not ready
- [ ] bump tutorial markdown to reference the smoke-check
- [ ] add test note to CHANGELOG / release notes draft

Quick developer commands for reviewer in PR description (pasteable):
- docker-compose -f examples/simple-chat/docker-compose.yaml pull && docker-compose up --build
- tail -n 200 examples/simple-chat/logs/model-server.log | grep -i "error\|ready"
- curl -sSf localhost:8080/health || echo "health failed"

Notes-to-self for docs gap items beyond this patch (lower priority):
- Add an explicit "runtime matrix" table: GPU tags vs CPU tags vs quantization compatibility. Link to Optimize guide.
- One-liner in quickstart about "When to use Dedicated vs Hosted for cost/latency tradeoffs" (small paragraph) — ask Product to review tone.
- Example prompts for batched inference: include a short snippet showing how to batch multiple small requests into a single call and where to enable caching keys.

Follow-ups and owners:
- Maya: review smoke-check script and CI feasibility (ask by EOD).
- Alex: sanity-check wording on Dedicated note and PR.
- Me (Quinn): open PR with hotfix + small CHANGELOG entry, link here.

Timebox notes:
- If I can't reproduce within 30m, pivot to adding informative error handling in README and filing an issue for infra to investigate. But try hard to repro first.

Random snippets / micro-brainstorm for future doc examples:
- "Minimal batch loop" js example: show Array.reduce to build batch, send single request, map responses back. Keep memory small (max tokens per batch).
- A debug troubleshooting section: "if you see ModelLoadError -> check runtime tag, quantization schema, and model sha mismatch (git submodule for model artifacts)."

Triage log (append as I go):
- 13:15 reproduced ModelLoadError locally.
- 13:35 changed image tag locally -> model server started, passed /health.
- 13:50 smoke-check script passes.
- 14:05 prepping PR: description + testing notes.

End-of-session TODO (next steps):
- Push PR and request Maya + Alex review. (PR link to paste here after creation)
- Update tutorial markdown and bump tutorial release notes draft.
- Add a short entry to the devx team's weekly update noting the runtime-tag caveat so other teams search-and-replace examples.

Tiny personal reminder: grab lunch earlier next time ¯\\_(ツ)_/¯
